title: Datum — Parametric Sketch Solver
description: An interactive geometric constraint solver in the spirit of Sutherland's Sketchpad. Sketch points, lines, circles, circular arcs AND cubic Bézier splines, then pin them together with real relations — coincident, horizontal/vertical, parallel, perpendicular, equal, tangent (line-to-arc, arc-to-arc, spline-to-line, spline-to-arc, and smooth G1 spline-to-spline joins), concentric, point-on-line/circle/arc, symmetric, colinear, midpoint, plus dimensional distance / angle / radius / diameter. Arcs and splines are first-class in the same 'everything reduces to points' spirit: an arc is a center, two endpoint points and a radius held by two intrinsic endpoint-on-circle residuals, and a cubic spline reduces to its four control points (start, two handles, end) carrying NO parameter of its own — so a free spline is just 8 draggable degrees of freedom and its endpoint tangents are the handle vectors, the basis of three tangency constraints that reuse the exact same parallel/perpendicular residual algebra the line and arc relations use. Draw an arc with a three-click center→start→end tool or a spline with a four-click control-point gesture, drag any handle and watch the curve re-fair live. Every relation becomes a scalar residual equation and the whole system is driven to zero by a from-scratch Levenberg–Marquardt least-squares solver. The Jacobian is EXACT: each residual is written once over an abstract arithmetic and re-run through a sparse forward-mode dual number, so the derivative is the residual code differentiated by the compiler — one source of truth, no finite-difference noise (a live differential test confirms it matches central differences to ~1e-8, arc and spline residuals included). Drag any point and the sketch re-solves live under your cursor; a Jacobian-rank degree-of-freedom analysis reports in real time whether the sketch is under-, well-, or over-constrained, and conflict diagnosis row-reduces the Jacobian to flag the SPECIFIC redundant constraints in red. One-click auto-constrain infers horizontal/vertical/parallel/perpendicular/equal/coincident from a rough drawing — admitting each only if it raises the rank, so it never over-constrains. Full undo/redo, save/open as JSON, and a shareable URL that reconstructs the whole sketch; double-click any dimension to retarget it. Fourteen worked examples DRIVE live, including the Peaucellier–Lipkin inversor (1864) that traces a mathematically EXACT straight line (held to ~1e-12 across its sweep), Hoeken's approximate four-bar for contrast, three arc showcases (a rounded slot, a tangent-arc fillet and a rounded rectangle, each fully constrained by one radius), and three spline showcases — a tangent S-curve with a smooth G1 join, a line-into-circle blend tangent to both, and a symmetric mirrored petal. And it doesn't just show WHERE a driven mechanism sits — it computes HOW FAST: an exact KINEMATICS engine reads the instantaneous velocity AND acceleration of every point straight off the constraint Jacobian. Holding the constraints fixed, the free parameters are an implicit function x(θ) of the driver, so ẋ = J⁺·e_driver (the first-order kinematic coefficient dx/dθ) and ẍ = J⁺·(−ẋᵀ∇²F ẋ) (the second-order coefficient d²x/dθ²) — the acceleration term coming from a genuine SECOND-ORDER forward-mode autodiff (hyper-dual numbers {value, 1st, 2nd directional derivative}) that is a third instantiation of the very same residual algebra, so there are still zero finite differences in the result. Toggle live cyan velocity and violet acceleration vector fields over the whole mechanism, read the traced point's speed and acceleration as both per-crank coefficients and true per-second rates, watch the drive gain diverge as the linkage nears a dead point, and read peak speed / peak acceleration off a live v(θ)/a(θ) profile plot swept over a full cycle. A 32-check live self-test suite re-derives every claim from an independent reference — the new kinematics checks proving the hyper-dual derivatives against the sparse-AD Jacobian to ~1e-16, the velocity/acceleration fields against finite differences of a re-solve, and a slider-crank against textbook closed-form kinematics.
